info.text: English for Aviation Maintenance — Unit 30: Mentoring: explaining a task to a junior (CEFR B2). Split by skill: Listening, Reading, Use of English, Vocabulary.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again — The walk-through. The mentor asks which important action comes before jacking the aircraft. What is the correct answer?

generalfeedback.text: The junior answers: the foreign object debris check, and reading the entire task card in the correct order. Both happen before the aircraft is lifted.

answer.text: Check for foreign object debris and read the task card.

feedback.text: Correct — both come before the aircraft is jacked.

answer.text: Lift the aircraft on the jack, then remove the old wheel.

feedback.text: No — jacking is the step in question, so it cannot come before itself.

answer.text: Set the torque wrench and confirm the specified value.

feedback.text: No — torque comes much later, after the new wheel is fitted.

answer.text: Fit the new lockwire around the hub and pull it tight.

feedback.text: No — the lockwire is the final step of the job.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. True or false: the junior has already changed a wheel alone, without close supervision.

generalfeedback.text: False. The junior says: "Although I have observed a wheel change before, this is my first without close supervision." Observing is not the same as doing it alone.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: No — the junior had only observed one before.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Correct — this is the junior's first without close supervision.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again — Torque, lockwire, and a deliberate error. What torque value, in newton metres, does the task card specify for the wheel nut? Enter the number only.

generalfeedback.text: 300. The junior reads: "The task card specifies three hundred newton metres for this particular wheel nut."

feedback.text: Correct — 300 Nm.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. After the nut is torqued, what stops it from turning loose?

generalfeedback.text: The lockwire — fitted through the nut and around the hub so it pulls the nut tight, never loose.

answer.text: The lockwire, fitted so it pulls the nut tight.

feedback.text: Correct — the lockwire secures the torqued nut.

answer.text: The ratchet, tightened firmly against the wheel hub.

feedback.text: No — a ratchet is the wrong tool and does not lock anything.

answer.text: A second nut, added on top to lock the first one.

feedback.text: No — no second nut is mentioned in the dialogue.

answer.text: The jack, holding steady pressure under the axle.

feedback.text: No — the jack lifts the aircraft; it does not hold the nut.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. True or false: the mentor says the lockwire may run in either direction.

generalfeedback.text: False. The mentor says: "The lockwire must always pull the nut tight, never loose." Direction matters.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: No — the junior assumed that, and the mentor corrected it.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Correct — the wire must pull the nut tight, never loose.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again — Checking understanding and sign-off authority. How many errors did the mentor say he had to correct during the wheel change? Enter the number only.

generalfeedback.text: 1. The mentor says: "Strong, ordered work, although I had to correct the lockwire direction once."

feedback.text: Correct — one error, the lockwire direction.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again. What does the mentor say sign-off authority requires?

generalfeedback.text: "Sign-off authority requires a valid licence and a formal competence assessment." Practice alone is not enough.

answer.text: A valid licence and a formal competence assessment.

feedback.text: Correct — both are named in the dialogue.

answer.text: A completed walk-through and a supervisor's spoken approval.

feedback.text: No — a spoken approval is not sign-off authority.

answer.text: More hands-on practice and a signed foreign-object check.

feedback.text: No — practice helps, but it is not the requirement stated.

answer.text: A finished wheel change and a full comprehension check.

feedback.text: No — those happened today, yet the junior still cannot sign off.

questiontext.text:
Read this note.

A Minimum Equipment List (MEL) item lets an aircraft fly with a named part inoperative for a limited time, if the stated conditions are met.

What does an MEL item allow?

generalfeedback.text: An MEL permits flight with a listed item inoperative, but only under set conditions and for a limited time — it is not permanent and not unconditional.

answer.text: Flight with a listed item inoperative, under set conditions.

feedback.text: Correct — limited time, stated conditions.

answer.text: Permanent removal of a part that is no longer needed at all.

feedback.text: No — the MEL is temporary, not a permanent removal.

answer.text: Any repair to be delayed until the next heavy maintenance check.

feedback.text: No — the time limit and conditions are much tighter than that.

answer.text: The crew to ignore a fault light for the rest of the aircraft's life.

feedback.text: No — nothing is ignored; conditions must be met.

questiontext.text:
Read this note.

A Service Bulletin (SB) is issued by the manufacturer and is usually recommended, not mandatory — unless an Airworthiness Directive makes it compulsory.

True or false: a Service Bulletin is always mandatory on its own.

generalfeedback.text: False. An SB is usually a recommendation. It becomes mandatory only when an Airworthiness Directive requires it.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: No — an SB is usually recommended, not compulsory.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Correct — only an AD can make it mandatory.

questiontext.text:
Read this note about avionics work.

A Built-In Test Equipment (BITE) readout on the avionics display shows fault codes stored by a system's self-test. The technician reads the code, then finds it in the fault-isolation manual.

What does a BITE readout give the technician?

generalfeedback.text: BITE shows stored fault codes from the system's own self-test. The technician still has to look the code up and act on it — the system does not repair itself.

answer.text: Stored fault codes from a system's self-test.

feedback.text: Correct — codes to look up in the manual.

answer.text: A direct repair, carried out automatically by the system.

feedback.text: No — BITE reports faults; it does not fix them.

answer.text: The full wiring diagram for the whole avionics bay.

feedback.text: No — that is a separate document, not the BITE readout.

answer.text: A spoken warning sent to the flight crew in the cockpit.

feedback.text: No — BITE is read by the technician on the display.

questiontext.text:
Read this note.

The technical log records every defect and the action taken. A deferred defect must be entered with its MEL reference.

True or false: a deferred defect is entered in the technical log with its MEL reference.

generalfeedback.text: True. The note states exactly that: a deferred defect must be entered with its MEL reference.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Correct — the MEL reference goes in the log.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: No — the note requires the MEL reference to be recorded.

questiontext.text:
Read this note.

An Airworthiness Directive (AD) is issued by the regulator, not the manufacturer, and compliance is mandatory by a stated deadline.

Who issues an AD, and is it mandatory?

generalfeedback.text: The regulator issues an AD, and compliance is mandatory by the stated deadline. An SB, by contrast, comes from the manufacturer and is usually only recommended.

answer.text: The regulator; compliance is mandatory by a deadline.

feedback.text: Correct — regulator-issued and compulsory.

answer.text: The manufacturer; it is only a recommendation to operators.

feedback.text: No — that describes a Service Bulletin, not an AD.

answer.text: The mentor; it applies only during on-the-job training.

feedback.text: No — an AD is a regulatory document, not a training note.

answer.text: The flight crew; it applies for one single flight only.

feedback.text: No — the crew do not issue ADs.

questiontext.text:
Change to a teaching imperative. Write the ONE word that fills the gap.

First, you fit the lockwire. → First, ______ the lockwire.

generalfeedback.text: A teaching step drops the subject and uses the plain verb: fit. "First, fit the lockwire."

answer.text: fit

feedback.text: Correct — the bare imperative.

answer.text: fit the lockwire

feedback.text: Accepted — the full imperative step.

questiontext.text:
Add the sequencer that marks the LAST step. Write one word.

______, fit the lockwire.

generalfeedback.text: Finally marks the last step: "Finally, fit the lockwire." (Also fine: Lastly.)

answer.text: Finally

feedback.text: Correct.

answer.text: Finally,

feedback.text: Correct.

answer.text: Lastly

feedback.text: Accepted.

questiontext.text:
Correct the sequencer error. Write the corrected opening word.

In first, read the task card. → ______, read the task card.

generalfeedback.text: English does not say "in first". The sequencer is just First: "First, read the task card."

answer.text: First

feedback.text: Correct — no "in".

answer.text: First,

feedback.text: Correct.

questiontext.text:
Rewrite this step with the two missing articles.

Put wheel on axle.

generalfeedback.text: Both parts are known, so each needs the: "Put the wheel on the axle." Latvian and Russian have no articles, so they are easy to drop.

answer.text: Put the wheel on the axle

feedback.text: Correct — both articles restored.

answer.text: Put the wheel on the axle.

feedback.text: Correct.

questiontext.text:
Complete the term. Write one word.

The tool that tightens a fastener to an exact value is a torque ______.

generalfeedback.text: wrench. A torque wrench tightens to an exact, specified value — you never guess it.

answer.text: wrench

feedback.text: Correct — a torque wrench.

questiontext.text:
Change to a teaching imperative. Write the ONE word that fills the gap.

Then, you are torquing the nut. → Then, ______ the nut.

generalfeedback.text: Use the plain verb, not the continuous: torque. "Then, torque the nut."

answer.text: torque

feedback.text: Correct — plain imperative.

answer.text: torque the nut

feedback.text: Accepted.

questiontext.text:
Complete the term from the vocabulary bank. Write one word.

The safety reason behind a step is the ______.

generalfeedback.text: rationale. A good mentor always gives the rationale, so the junior understands why the step matters.

answer.text: rationale

feedback.text: Correct.

questiontext.text: Match each term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: mentor = an experienced technician who guides a junior; lockwire = wire that stops a fastener turning loose; axle = the shaft the wheel turns on; airworthiness = the state of being safe and legal to fly; task card = the card that lists the steps of one job.

partiallycorrectfeedback.text: Some pairs are right — check the rest.

incorrectfeedback.text: Review the meanings in the vocabulary bank and try again.

answer.text: an experienced technician who guides a junior
wire that stops a fastener turning loose
the shaft the wheel turns on
the state of being safe and legal to fly
the card that lists the steps of one job

questiontext.text: Match each term to the verb phrase it completes.

generalfeedback.text: give a walk-through; build competence; set the torque wrench; protect airworthiness; check for foreign object debris. Learning the natural partner word makes B2 speech fluent.

partiallycorrectfeedback.text: Some are right — check the rest against the vocabulary bank.

incorrectfeedback.text: Review the collocation column in the vocabulary bank.

answer.text: give a ___
build ___
set the ___
protect ___
check for ___

questiontext.text: Which phrase is the correct collocation for a demonstration of a task?

generalfeedback.text: We give a walk-through. English pairs "give" with walk-through, demonstration and feedback.

answer.text: give a walk-through

feedback.text: Correct — the natural collocation.

answer.text: make a walk-through slowly

feedback.text: No — "make" is not used with walk-through.

answer.text: open a walk-through first

feedback.text: No — "open" does not collocate here.

answer.text: do a walk-through for me

feedback.text: No — "give a walk-through" is the fixed phrase.

questiontext.text: Choose the best meaning of competence in this unit.

generalfeedback.text: Competence is proven ability to do a task correctly and safely. It grows with supervised practice and is confirmed by a formal assessment.

answer.text: Proven ability to do a task correctly and safely.

feedback.text: Correct.

answer.text: A strong wish to finish the task before the others do.

feedback.text: No — that confuses competence with competition.

answer.text: Permission to certify that a job is fully complete.

feedback.text: No — that is sign-off authority, not competence.

answer.text: The tool used to tighten a nut to a set value.

feedback.text: No — that is a torque wrench.
